name: Medical Exam Gloves
description: Size the market for disposable medical exam gloves.
formula: SAM = Population x Penetration Rate x Purchase Frequency x Average Spend x Serviceable %
solution_logic: Step 1: Identify addressable population = target_population x addressable_segment
Step 2: Apply penetration rate = addressable_population x penetration_rate
Step 3: Calculate annual spend per user = purchase_frequency x avg_spend_per_purchase
Step 4: Calculate TAM = penetrating_users x annual_spend_per_user
Step 5: Calculate SAM = TAM x serviceable_pct
key_insight: The population is hospitals and clinics, not patients or the general public -- this is a B2B procurement market sized by facility count and order value, not population health metrics.
common_mistakes: Sizing by patient population or general public instead of the number of hospitals & clinics
Treating orders/year as a soft assumption when it's structurally fixed by standard procurement cycles
Ignoring current distribution reach (serviceable %), which caps who this manufacturer can actually sell to today
framework_soundbite: Facilities, not patients; standard procurement cycles, not annual bulk buys -- the population here is B2B, not B2C.
business_contexts: a medical supply manufacturer evaluating a new glove production line
a hospital procurement group sizing annual glove demand
question_patterns: A medical supply manufacturer is deciding whether to add a new glove production line and wants to size the serviceable portion of annual demand it could actually distribute to.

prompts.advanced: A contract manufacturer is being asked to commit capital to a new glove production line based on a distributor's demand forecast that leadership suspects is optimistic. Build an independent view of the serviceable addressable market before approving the capex.
prompts.beginner: Estimate the serviceable addressable market for disposable medical exam gloves within the manufacturer's current distribution reach.
prompts.intermediate: A medical supply manufacturer is deciding whether to add a new glove production line and wants to size the serviceable portion of annual demand it could actually distribute to.

approach_guidance.top_down_why: Start from hospitals & clinics, narrow to those using disposable gloves, apply penetration and current distribution reach, then multiply by order value -- narrowing down from the facility count.
approach_guidance.bottom_up_why: Or start from one facility: its annual order value (orders/year x $/order), then scale up by how many penetrating, glove-using facilities this manufacturer's distribution reaches. The more natural default -- B2B procurement is usually sized bottom-up from one account's order value, not down from a population.
